To the testing house's representative, on behalf of the design owner:

The current draft doesn't work for either side as written. "Any adviser" is too open for us, and a flat ban on copies is unworkable for you, since you can't build fixtures or run analysis without working files. On-demand audit access is also more intrusive than it needs to be. Here is a package that loosens the last two in exchange for tightening the first.

**1. Disclosure (replaces "any adviser")**

> "The Testing House shall disclose the Drawings only to those of its personnel named in Schedule 1 who need access to perform the Tests. Additions to Schedule 1 require the Designer's prior written consent, not to be unreasonably withheld or delayed. Disclosure to any external adviser or subcontractor requires the Designer's prior written consent and that person's written undertaking of confidentiality on terms no less protective than this Agreement. The Testing House remains liable for any breach by a person to whom it discloses the Drawings."

**2. Copies and fixtures (replaces the bar on all copies)**

> "The Testing House may make such working copies of the Drawings as are reasonably necessary to perform the Tests, provided each copy is stored and transmitted in encrypted form and accessed only by Schedule 1 personnel. The Testing House may design and manufacture test fixtures and adaptors derived from the Drawings ('Derivative Fixtures') solely for the Tests. Within 14 days after the Designer's written acceptance of the test report, the Testing House shall permanently destroy or delete all copies of the Drawings and all Derivative Fixtures, together with any models, CAD files or tooling data from which the geometry could be reconstructed."

**3. Verification (replaces audit on demand)**

> "Within 7 days after destruction, the Testing House shall deliver a certificate of destruction issued by an independent third party acceptable to both parties, acting reasonably, confirming the destruction of the items in clause [2]. The cost of certification shall be borne by [ ]."

We would give up site access entirely in return for this. We'd suggest splitting the certifier's cost equally, but are open on that.

**4. Use restriction (new)**

> "The Testing House shall use the Drawings, Derivative Fixtures and any information derived from them solely to perform the Tests for the Designer, and shall not use them, directly or indirectly, to design, develop or assist in the development of any product competing with the Designer's actuators, whether for itself or any third party."

Points where we need your input:

- **Names for Schedule 1.** How many people realistically need access, and do you use any outside labs or contract machinists for fixture manufacture? If so, we'd rather deal with them by name now than through consent requests later.
- **Retention you actually need.** If accreditation or quality rules require you to keep test records, tell us what. We can accept retention of test data and reports that don't reproduce the geometry; we can't accept retained drawings or fixture models.
- **Fixture destruction.** If destroying physical fixtures is a cost issue for you, an alternative we could consider is delivering them to us instead of destroying them.
- **Timing.** 14 days and 7 days are proposals; say so if your shutdown process needs longer.

The named-personnel requirement, equivalent confidentiality terms for anyone outside, proof of destruction, and the non-compete use restriction are the terms that matter most to us. The mechanics around them are flexible.

We can accept named access, equivalent confidentiality undertakings, the 14-day and 7-day deadlines, and a restriction on competitive use of the drawings. We propose two attachments and the following verification terms.

**Schedule 1 — People and specialists.** We use a specialist machining shop for fixture manufacture and an accredited lab for vibration testing. Before any release, we will submit the two legal names, the lab’s accreditation scope, and a roster identifying each person who needs access, their employer and their task. The headcount will follow that roster. We propose this wording for approval and substitution.

> Approval of Schedule 1 authorizes each listed person to receive only the material allocated to their task in Schedule 2. Before disclosure, each specialist shall give a written undertaking covering confidentiality, permitted use, restricted access and disposal on terms at least as protective as this agreement, and shall bind its listed personnel to those terms. The Testing House remains responsible for their compliance.
>
> The Testing House may propose a replacement person or specialist by email, identifying the proposed recipient, qualifications, task and material required. The Designer shall approve or give reasonable written grounds for objection within three business days. Email approval updates Schedule 1. Access begins only upon written approval. The Testing House shall revoke the outgoing recipient’s access when its task ends and obtain written confirmation of return or destruction of its copies.

**Schedule 2 — Release and disposition.** We propose listing each authorized extract by identifier and revision, with its recipient, purpose and disposition. The shop receives only the interfaces and dimensions needed to machine its fixture. The lab receives only the mounting and setup extracts needed to run the tests. Both may make necessary controlled working copies. Electronic copies must be encrypted in storage and transit, and any shop-floor print must be numbered, secured and recovered for destruction.

> Within 14 days after written acceptance of the report or earlier termination of the work, the Testing House shall delete or destroy all drawings, extracts, working copies and files from which the geometry can be reconstructed, including those held by specialists. The Designer may elect in writing by acceptance or termination to have physical fixtures delivered to it at its freight cost. Otherwise the Testing House shall destroy them. The Testing House may retain calibration records for two years for quality and accreditation purposes, provided they contain no drawings, dimensions or other information from which geometry can be reconstructed.

**Verification.** We accept giving up site access entirely. In exchange, we propose routine certification by our responsible manager, with independent review available if the evidence leaves a specific question unresolved.

> Within seven days after completing disposal, the Testing House shall provide a signed attestation reconciling each Schedule 2 entry to its deletion, destruction or delivery, supported by specialist confirmations and delivery receipts where applicable. If the Designer identifies a specific discrepancy that the Testing House cannot resolve with documentary evidence, either party may request confidential remote review by a mutually acceptable independent reviewer. Review shall be limited to relevant records, with other customers’ information redacted, and shall confer no right of site entry. The parties shall share the review cost equally unless the reviewer confirms material noncompliance by the Testing House, in which case the Testing House shall bear it.

**Use restriction.** We propose tying the competitive-use restriction to the protected material so that we can continue independent testing work.

> The Testing House shall use the drawings, extracts, derivative fixtures and information derived from them solely to perform the agreed tests and meet the recordkeeping and verification obligations above. It shall not use that material to design, develop or assist in developing a competing actuator. The Testing House may apply independently developed testing methods and general skills on other engagements without using or disclosing that material.

Can you accept manager attestation backed by specialist confirmations as the routine proof, with independent review on the discrepancy terms above, and the three-business-day written decision for substitutions?

Most of this is agreed. Verification is the one term we can't take as drafted.

**Agreed**
- **Schedule 1 mechanics and three-business-day substitutions.** One clarification: "Silence is not approval."
- **Schedule 2 release by extract, identifier and revision.** Numbered prints are agreed, with two additions:
  - "Native CAD models shall be held only by the Testing House's listed personnel and shall not be released to any specialist."
  - "No specialist may disclose onward."
- **Disposition.** The termination trigger, fixture delivery at our freight cost and two-year retention of geometry-free calibration records are agreed. Please add "including backup and archive copies" to the deletion duty.

**Verification — counter**

Manager attestation alone is the Testing House certifying itself. The discrepancy trigger also asks us to spot a problem in records we cannot see. We have given up site access, so we need an independent check as routine. It can be light and remote.

> Within seven days after completing disposal, the Testing House shall provide (a) a signed attestation by its responsible manager reconciling each Schedule 2 entry to its deletion, destruction or delivery, supported by specialist confirmations and delivery receipts, and (b) a certificate from a mutually acceptable independent reviewer confirming, from a confidential remote review of the reconciliation, deletion logs, print register and specialist confirmations, that the attestation is supported by the records. The review shall be limited to records relating to this engagement, with other customers' information redacted, and shall confer no right of site entry. The Designer shall bear the cost of the routine certificate. If the reviewer finds material noncompliance, the Testing House shall bear that cost and the cost of any follow-up review.

This keeps your structure and scope limits. We take on the routine cost, so you bear cost only if something is wrong. The reviewer can be named in Schedule 1 now so that timing is not at risk.

**Use restriction — two edits**

> ...It shall not use that material, for itself or any third party, to design, develop or assist in developing a competing actuator or any component of one. The Testing House may apply independently developed testing methods and general skills on other engagements, provided it does not use or disclose that material, including any geometry, dimensions or design features of the Designer's actuator learned from it.

**One addition**

> The Testing House shall notify the Designer within two business days of becoming aware of any unauthorized access to, or loss of, protected material, including at a specialist.

Can you accept routine independent certification on those terms, at our cost, along with the two edits and the notice clause? If so, send the roster and the two specialists' names and we will turn to the Schedules.

We accept routine independent certification on the terms proposed. Within seven days after completing disposal, we will provide both the manager’s attestation and the reviewer’s certificate. The Designer will pay for the routine review. If the reviewer finds material noncompliance, we will pay for that review and any follow-up review. Verification will be remote, with no right of site entry.

We also accept both edits to the use restriction and the two-business-day notice clause, including incidents at either specialist. Silence does not approve a substitution. Native CAD stays with listed Testing House personnel, specialists may not disclose onward, and the deletion duty includes backup and archive copies.

The individual names, the specialists’ legal names and the lab’s accreditation scope are pending confirmation. We propose recording the following access limits in the schedules now.

| Schedule 1 entry | Schedule 2 access |
|---|---|
| Named Testing House personnel | Drawings and working files required for each person’s assigned task. Native CAD access identified individually. |
| Machining shop and named personnel | Controlled extracts of the interfaces and dimensions needed to manufacture the fixture. |
| Accredited lab and named personnel | Controlled mounting and setup extracts needed to run the vibration tests. |
| Mutually approved independent reviewer | Engagement-specific disposal records for verification, with other customers’ information redacted. No drawing access. |

Before the first release, we will submit the completed roster, the two legal names and the lab’s accreditation scope for written approval. Schedule 2 will identify each released extract by identifier and revision and link it to its named recipients, task and required disposition.

The schedule framework is accepted, and with it the terms are agreed in substance. Three points to record so the schedules close cleanly:

1. **No release before approval.** Add to Schedule 1: "No drawing, extract or working file shall be released to any person or specialist until the Designer has approved in writing the completed roster, the specialists' legal names and the lab's accreditation scope, and each specialist's signed undertaking has been delivered to the Designer."
2. **Native CAD access.** We expect the individually identified native CAD list to be limited to those who prepare the extracts and any fixture design. Each roster entry should give the reason that person needs native access, so we can approve on the first submission.
3. **Reviewer.** The reviewer row is agreed, including no drawing access. The reviewer should sign a confidentiality undertaking covering the disposal records, and should be named in the same roster submission so the seven-day certificate deadline is achievable.

On that basis, the agreed position is:

- **Disclosure:** only to Schedule 1 persons, with equivalent undertakings from both specialists and no onward disclosure.
- **Substitutions:** written decision within three business days, and silence is not approval.
- **Copies:** encrypted working copies and numbered prints. Specialists receive extracts only, and native CAD stays with listed Testing House personnel.
- **Disposal:** within 14 days of acceptance or termination, including backups and archives. Fixtures are destroyed, or delivered to the Designer at its freight cost if it so elects.
- **Retention:** geometry-free calibration records for two years.
- **Verification:** manager attestation plus an independent reviewer's certificate within seven days of disposal. Review is remote with no site entry. The Designer pays for the routine review, and the Testing House pays if material noncompliance is found.
- **Use:** solely for the agreed tests. No use for a competing actuator or component, for itself or any third party, with the general-skills carve-out as edited.
- **Incidents:** notice within two business days, including incidents at a specialist.

Send the roster, legal names, accreditation scope and proposed reviewer when confirmed, and we will respond within the three-business-day window.

We accept the proposed Schedule 1 release clause as written. We will limit native CAD access to named Testing House personnel who prepare extracts or design fixtures. Each request for native access will identify the person’s task and explain why it requires the native file.

We will include the proposed reviewer in the same roster submission and obtain the reviewer’s signed confidentiality undertaking before providing any disposal records. The reviewer will have no drawing access.

The roster, the two specialists’ legal names, the lab’s accreditation scope and the reviewer’s identity are pending confirmation. We will submit them together with both specialists’ signed undertakings. Release will begin only after the Designer’s written approval.

The festival wants to consider the film, but the draft's blanket ban on copying and on disclosure until public release would prevent us from reviewing it at all. Here are the specific carve-outs we need, each with the limits we can commit to.

**1. Who gets access**
- Five named people: four festival programmers and one outside accessibility reviewer.
- We provide the names in advance, and each is bound in writing to the same confidentiality terms.
- Nobody is added without your written approval.

**2. Offline screeners (copying exception)**
- Two of the five review offline, so we need permission for two downloaded copies.
- These sit only on encrypted equipment, with no further copies or transfers.
- They are deleted, with written confirmation, within a set period after the decision; we suggest 7 days.
- The other three stream only.
- If you want, we can accept individual watermarking of every screener.

**3. Platform backup**
- Our screener platform automatically keeps a backup for 30 days after a file is removed.
- We can't shorten that, so the agreement needs to acknowledge it instead of requiring immediate destruction.
- We can commit that the backup is not accessed or restored, stays under the confidentiality terms, and is purged at the end of the cycle.

**4. Synopsis to the selection board (disclosure exception)**
- The selection board must hear a short oral synopsis in order to decide.
- No footage or written materials would be circulated to the board, and its members are under festival confidentiality.
- If you prefer, you can supply or pre-approve the synopsis text.

**5. Catalog drafting**
- If the film is selected, we need permission to prepare catalog copy internally before the announcement.
- Nothing is published or shared outside the festival until the official announcement.
- You can review the copy before it goes out.

**Open questions for you**
- Does "public release" in the draft mean the film's release or the festival's announcement? We need the publicity restriction to lift at the announcement if the film is selected; otherwise the catalog itself would be a breach.
- Is watermarking or a pre-approved synopsis something you require, or is the commitment above enough?
- Is the 30-day backup acceptable as described?
- Does anything on your side need approval from a third party, such as a sales agent, financier or distributor, before you can agree to these exceptions?

If these five carve-outs work in principle, I'd propose we add them as a limited-purpose review exception to the existing draft and leave the rest of it intact.

The structure works: a limited-purpose review exception added to the draft, with the rest intact. Most of your points are agreed with conditions, and two need rights-holder confirmation before I can commit.

- The four named programmers, bound in writing, with no additions without our written approval, are agreed.
- The outside accessibility reviewer needs confirmation, because the rights holder's clearance covers named reviewing staff. I'll seek it; please send the name and affiliation, and say whether this person is one of the two offline reviewers. Stream-only would be easier to clear.

  - written confirmation of the purge date when the cycle ends;
  - immediate notice to us if the backup is accessed or restored for any reason.
- Please confirm whether the backup is encrypted and who at the platform vendor can technically reach it. I'll be asked.

**4. Synopsis to the board: agreed, on our text**
- We will supply the synopsis, and the oral briefing stays within it.
- The ending and one cast appearance (a cameo) are excluded and may not be disclosed to the board, including in answers to questions. We have a commitment to a financing party on this, so it is fixed.
- The five reviewers will see both, so their undertakings need to name these two items specifically.

**5. Catalog and publicity: agreed, with approval rights**
- Internal drafting before the announcement is fine.
- We approve all catalog and publicity copy before it leaves the festival, and we will respond within two business days of receipt. Silence is not approval.
- Excerpts, stills and clips come only from material we supply or approve in advance, with no frame grabs or quotes taken from screeners.
- The cameo performer is omitted from any cast listing, and the copy cannot describe or hint at the ending.

**Embargo trigger**

  - **At the festival's official announcement, if selected:** the restriction lifts for the approved copy and approved excerpts only.
  - **Until the film's public release:** the ending and cameo stay confidential, as does everything else about the unfinished cut, including reviewers' assessments.
- If the film is not selected, nothing lifts, and the fact that it was considered stays confidential.

**Withdrawal**
The producer may need to pull a cut at short notice, so we need the following:
- On our written notice, streaming access ends immediately.
- Offline copies are deleted within 48 hours, with the same deletion record.
- The 30-day backup clock starts on the day of removal.
- Withdrawing a cut does not withdraw the film. A replacement cut can go in under the same terms and to the same named reviewers.
- If the film itself is withdrawn before the announcement, the festival makes no statement. If after, we agree the wording jointly.

**Questions for you**
- Can your platform cut streaming access immediately and meet 48-hour offline deletion?
- Do you accept the two-tier embargo?
- Do you accept that silence within the two business days is not deemed approval? If you need certainty for print deadlines, tell me the dates and I'll get clearance scheduled around them.
- If the film is selected, festival screenings will show the ending to audiences and press. I suggest we handle spoiler requests in the selection agreement, not here, unless you prefer otherwise.

**Approvals still outstanding on our side**
Only two: the outside accessibility reviewer and the 30-day backup, both with the rights holder. Everything else above I can commit to now.

Most of this is accepted. Four operational facts need confirming with the festival before I can commit, and there is one gap in your embargo that I need closed.

**Accepted now**
- **Access:** four programmers plus the reviewer once cleared, with written undertakings that name the ending and the cameo specifically.
- **Offline copies:** a signed deletion record for each copy (reviewer, device, date, method) within 7 days of the decision.
- **Watermarking:** individual watermarks on all five screeners.
- **Synopsis:** your text only, with the ending and cameo excluded, including in answers to board questions.
- **Catalog and publicity:**
  - your approval before anything leaves the festival;
  - only supplied or approved excerpts, stills and clips;
  - no frame grabs or screener quotes;
  - the cameo performer left out of cast listings, and no hint of the ending.
- **Backup additions:** written confirmation of the purge date, and immediate notice if the backup is accessed or restored.
- **Withdrawal:**

  - the backup clock starts on removal.
- **Spoilers at festival screenings:** handled in the selection agreement, not here.

**Two-tier embargo: accepted, with one carve-out**
As drafted, "reviewers' assessments" stay confidential until release, which would stop the programmers from reporting to the selection board at all. I need the following:
- The five reviewers may discuss the cut among themselves.
- The programmers may give the board their recommendations and evaluative views, never disclosing the ending or the cameo.
- The accessibility reviewer may report findings to the programmers and to you.
- Nothing evaluative goes outside the festival before the film's release.

I'd also add the usual exceptions for disclosure required by law and for information you or the rights holder make public yourselves.

**Silence is not approval: accepted, with a safeguard**
- If the two business days pass without a response, the festival may hold or omit the entry without being in breach, and you will still respond promptly.
- I'll send the print and announcement deadlines once I have them, so clearance can be scheduled around them.

**To be confirmed on our side**
1. **Accessibility reviewer:** the name and affiliation, and whether this person is one of the two offline reviewers. I'll also ask whether stream-only is workable for them, since that is easier for you to clear.
2. **Backup:** whether it is encrypted and who at the vendor can technically reach it.

4. **48-hour offline deletion:** workable in principle, but it depends on reaching two individuals. I propose the clock runs from your written notice to a designated festival contact, and I'll confirm that the festival can meet it.

**What remains open**
- **Your side:** rights-holder clearance for the accessibility reviewer and for the 30-day backup.
- **My side:** the four confirmations above, plus the deadline dates.
- **Between us:** your agreement to the internal-deliberation carve-out and the hold-or-omit safeguard.

Access cannot start until both rights-holder clearances are in and the undertakings are signed. If the reviewer's clearance is the slower of the two, would you let the four programmers begin once the backup is cleared?

Both items between us are agreed, with the tightening below, and the phased start works.

**Internal-deliberation carve-out: agreed**
- The five reviewers may discuss the cut among themselves.
- The programmers may give the board recommendations and evaluative views, never disclosing the ending or the cameo.
- The accessibility reviewer may report findings to the programmers and to us.

- One clarification: your original point 4 said no written materials go to the board. If any recommendation is put in writing, it must stay inside the festival and omit both protected items.

**Standard exceptions: agreed, with two limits**
- **Required by law:** agreed, provided you give us prompt prior notice where lawful and disclose only the minimum required.
- **Information made public:** this applies only to the specific information that we or the rights holder have officially released. Leaks, rumor or third-party speculation about the ending or the cameo do not release anyone, and neither does our announcing other details about the film.

**Hold-or-omit safeguard: agreed**
- If two business days pass without our response, the festival may hold or omit the entry without breach, and we will still respond promptly.

**48-hour deletion clock: agreed**
- The clock runs from our written notice to a designated festival contact.
- Please name a primary and an alternate contact, so that one person's absence doesn't stall the clock.
- If a reviewer cannot be reached within the window, the festival tells us immediately and keeps that device unused and secured until deletion is recorded.

**Phased start: yes**
The four programmers may begin before the accessibility reviewer is cleared, once all of the following are in place:
- rights-holder clearance of the backup;
- your confirmation that streaming access can be ended immediately on our notice;
- signed undertakings from the four, naming the ending and the cameo;
- individual watermarks applied.

Offline downloads have one further condition: your confirmation that the festival can meet the 48-hour deletion. Until then the programmers stream only. If the accessibility reviewer is one of the two offline reviewers, that copy waits for their clearance.

**What remains open**
- **Our side:** rights-holder clearance for the backup and for the accessibility reviewer. I can't put the backup to the rights holder properly until I have your answers on encryption and vendor access, so those come first.
- **Your side:** the four confirmations, the two contact names and the deadline dates.

Nothing else is open between us. Once those items are in, the exception can be drafted as agreed.

All of your tightenings are accepted, so nothing remains to negotiate between us.

**Accepted**
- **Written recommendations:** any that exist stay inside the festival and omit the ending and the cameo.
- **Required by law:** prompt prior notice to you where lawful, and only the minimum disclosed.
- **Information made public:** limited to the specific information you or the rights holder officially release. Leaks, rumor, speculation and your announcing other details release nothing.
- **Hold or omit:** this never extends to publishing unapproved copy.
- **Unreachable reviewer:** we notify you immediately, and the device stays unused and secured until deletion is recorded.
- **Phased start:** the four programmers begin on your four conditions and stream only until we confirm the 48-hour deletion. If the accessibility reviewer is one of the offline two, that copy waits for their clearance.

**What I owe you, in this order**
1. Whether the backup is encrypted and who at the vendor can reach it, since your backup clearance depends on these.
2. Confirmation that streaming access can be ended immediately on your notice.
3. Confirmation that the festival can meet the 48-hour offline deletion.
4. The accessibility reviewer's name and affiliation, and whether they review offline or can be stream-only.

We propose replacing the blanket approval requirement with the following terms for the three-depot trial.

1. **Raw failure traces and firmware parameters.** Only designated members of the two project teams who need these materials for trial work may access them. Neither party may share them with an external maintenance contractor, including in a report or support ticket, except under the safety provision below. The teams may share other measurements internally with staff who need them to operate or evaluate the trial.

2. **External reports.** The reporting party will give the other party a draft at least 10 working days before release. During that period, the reviewer may identify specific passages that expose restricted information or contain a material factual error. The reporting party will remove restricted information and correct verified errors. If a passage remains disputed, the reporting party may release the rest. Once the review period expires, release may proceed without affirmative approval.

3. **Aggregate uptime.** We may publish uptime combined across all three depots after the same review period. We will omit route and depot identifiers and any breakdown that would allow readers to identify a route or depot. The teams will agree on the uptime calculation before the first report so both can verify the figure.

4. **Urgent safety disclosures.** Either party may immediately disclose the minimum information needed to address an urgent safety risk to someone able to act on it. The disclosing party will notify the other as soon as practicable afterward, identifying what it shared, with whom, and why.

What maintenance decision, if any, requires the external contractor to see a raw trace? We propose giving the contractor a fault summary and recommended action first. If that leaves a specific task unresolved, we can test whether a trial-team engineer can answer the contractor’s diagnostic question while keeping the raw trace within the team.

Your structure works for us with changes to four points. Clause 2's deemed approval after the review period and clause 3's agreed uptime calculation are accepted as written.

**1. Contractor access (your question).**
We can't point to a specific maintenance decision that requires a raw trace today, so we accept summary-first. What we need is a guarantee that a repair doesn't stall, so we propose three tiers:

- **Tier 1, standard fault package.** The contractor receives the fault code, affected component, device ID, fault time rounded to the shift, the conditions needed to reproduce the fault, and the recommended action. This is not treated as restricted material and may go into support tickets.
- **Tier 2, engineer answers.** If the task is unresolved, a trial-team engineer answers the contractor's diagnostic question within one working day, or four hours if the device is out of service at a depot.
- **Tier 3, trace excerpt.** If the task is still unresolved after that window, the relevant trace excerpt goes to named contractor technicians under a written confidentiality undertaking, for that repair only, and is deleted on closure. Firmware parameters stay excluded unless your engineer agrees they are needed.

If you have a different response window in mind for Tier 2, propose one. We need a fixed number in the text.

**2. Safety and regulatory disclosures.**
Clause 4 is too narrow for us. Our safety lead has to notify authorities promptly about serious incidents and cannot make that subject to clearance or to a contested "minimum" test. We propose replacing it with:

> Nothing in this agreement restricts either party from reporting a serious incident or safety risk to a regulator, investigator, emergency service or other competent authority, or from providing information those bodies request, including raw traces. No prior notice or approval is required. The disclosing party will tell the other within two working days what was shared, with whom and why, unless the authority prohibits it, and will mark the material as commercially confidential where the authority's process allows.

Your "minimum necessary" standard can stay for urgent disclosures to non-authorities, such as a depot manager or the contractor.

**3. Monthly board reporting.**
Our board needs aggregate results every month, and a 10-working-day review per issue doesn't fit that cycle. We propose that the teams agree a fixed report template and metric definitions before the first report. Reports that stay within the template then issue without per-issue review, with a copy to you at the same time. Anything outside the template goes through clause 2 review.

**4. Employee-identifying data.**
Exact depot and time pairs can identify individual employees. We propose that this applies to both parties and to all external reports, not only uptime:

- No release may contain depot-plus-timestamp combinations or any breakdown finer than a calendar month across the three depots combined.
- This is the one category where a disputed passage is withheld rather than released. We make the final call on whether a passage identifies an employee.

**5. Who approves.**
Each party names a project lead who receives drafts, raises objections and signs off on the template. Our safety lead alone decides on disclosures under the authority clause above. For your marketing or public use of trial results beyond aggregate uptime, we propose keeping the clause 2 process, with our project lead as reviewer.

Two things we need from you: can you accept the authority clause as drafted, and what Tier 2 response window can your engineers commit to?

Yes. We accept your authority clause as drafted, including the two-working-day notice provision. We also accept a Tier 2 response window of **one working day, shortened to four elapsed hours when a device is out of service at a depot**. We propose the following text to close the remaining points.

1. **Contractor support.** The contractor may receive the Tier 1 fields you listed in a repair ticket. Reproduction conditions must be described without revealing raw traces or firmware parameters. The trial team will provide a monitored contact for Tier 2 questions. The response clock starts when that contact receives the question. Within the applicable window, our engineer will provide a diagnostic answer or, if the cause is still unknown, a specific next repair or diagnostic step and a time for the next update. If the task remains unresolved at the deadline, our engineer will work directly with the named technician, inspect the trace within the trial team, and relay findings through the ticket. Raw traces, including excerpts, and firmware parameters remain within the trial team during routine repairs. The safety exceptions apply independently.

2. **Safety decisions.** Your safety lead decides on authority disclosures made on your behalf. Our designated safety lead has the same role for disclosures on ours. Either party may immediately share the minimum information needed with a non-authority able to act on an urgent risk. It will tell the other party what it shared, with whom and why as soon as practicable afterward.

3. **Monthly board reports.** Both project leads will approve the template and metric definitions before first use. You may send each conforming report to your board without per-issue review and copy us at the same time. The board will receive it in confidence. Any additional material goes through clause 2. Public release of a board report also goes through clause 2.

4. **Employee privacy.** For both parties’ external reports and the monthly board report, results must combine all three depots and use periods of one calendar month or longer. Reports must omit route and depot identifiers, depot-plus-timestamp pairs, and details that would identify an employee. Your project lead has final say on employee identification and will flag the passage and explain the concern. The reporting party will withhold that passage until it is revised to resolve the concern and may release the rest on schedule. These reporting limits leave the agreed repair-ticket and safety provisions available for their stated purposes.

5. **Review and publication.** Each party will name one project lead to receive drafts, raise specific objections and approve the board template. We may publish aggregate uptime using the agreed calculation and privacy limits after the 10-working-day review. Our other public or marketing uses of trial results follow clause 2 with your project lead as reviewer. The review period runs from receipt of the draft and expires without further sign-off, subject to the agreed rules for restricted material, factual corrections and employee privacy.

Does direct engineer support at Tier 3, with a concrete next step due within the fixed Tier 2 window, meet your repair requirement?

Direct engineer support at Tier 3 meets our repair requirement, and raw traces and firmware parameters can stay within the trial team for routine repairs, provided two additions go into clause 1:

- **Sufficiency of relayed findings.** The engineer's findings in the ticket must include whatever specific detail the technician needs to complete the repair, such as the failing component, measured values, thresholds or the sequence of events, even where that detail is derived from a trace. The restriction covers the trace itself and firmware parameters, not conclusions drawn from them.
- **Backstop for a device out of service.** If a device is still out of service three working days after the Tier 2 question was received, you will repair or replace it yourselves, on site or by swap, at your cost. Without a trace excerpt as the last resort, we need a fixed end point of this kind.

Clauses 2, 4 and 5 are accepted as drafted.

Clause 3 is accepted with two changes:

- **Legally required disclosure.** "The board will receive it in confidence" needs the qualifier "subject to any disclosure the operator or its board is required by law to make." We can't commit the board beyond its legal obligations. If such a disclosure is required, we will tell you promptly and release only the conforming report.
- **Public release of a conforming report.** Because the template and metrics are already approved and the report meets the clause 4 limits, we propose that review is limited to confirming conformity and runs five working days instead of 10. Additional material stays on the full clause 2 process.

If you accept these four changes, we have an agreed text on our side. If the three-day backstop is the difficulty, propose the period and remedy you can commit to.

We accept all four changes. The three-working-day repair backstop and the five-working-day review for public release of a conforming board report are agreed. The following additions complete clauses 1 and 3.

**Clause 1 — Contractor support**

The engineer will record in the repair ticket the specific findings the technician needs to complete the repair. These may include the failing component, measured values, diagnostic thresholds and the sequence of events, including findings derived from a trace. Raw traces, trace excerpts and firmware parameters remain within the trial team for routine repairs. If a repair depends on a threshold that is itself a firmware parameter, the engineer will report the measured value, whether it crossed the threshold and the action the technician should take.

If the device is still out of service three working days after the trial team received the Tier 2 question, we will take over the repair at that point and repair or replace the device at our cost, on site or by swap. Escalation to Tier 3 does not restart the clock.

**Clause 3 — Monthly board reports**

The board will receive each conforming report in confidence, subject to any disclosure the operator or its board is required by law to make. For a legally required disclosure of the report, the operator will notify us promptly and release only the conforming report. The agreed authority-disclosure clause continues to apply to incident reporting and authority requests.

For voluntary public release of a conforming board report, the operator will send the report to our project lead five working days before release. Review is limited to confirming conformity with the approved template, metric definitions and clause 4 privacy limits. The operator may release a conforming report at the end of that period without further sign-off. Any additional material follows the full 10-working-day review.

Both additions are accepted as drafted, including the firmware-threshold wording in clause 1 and the conformity-only review in clause 3. On our side the text is agreed in full: clauses 1 to 5 as last stated, plus the authority-disclosure clause as we drafted it.

The remaining steps are operational and can be done before the first report:

- each party names its project lead and safety lead,
- you supply the monitored Tier 2 contact,
- we supply the named contractor technicians,
- the project leads approve the board template, metric definitions and uptime calculation.

We'd like to tighten the three open clauses in the draft schedule, and here is what the studio proposes for each.

**1. Subcontractors**

The draft's general permission is broader than we need. We'd replace it with one named subcontractor: an external color specialist, used for the first batch only.

- **Scope:** color calibration only, with no other use of the materials.
- **Terms:** the specialist signs confidentiality terms no less strict than this schedule, and the studio remains fully liable for their handling.
- **Additions:** any other subcontractor requires the archive's prior written consent.
- **Access:** we'd prefer the specialist work from master images, because full frames give better calibration than crops. Transfer would be encrypted, with no local copies kept past the calibration task and written deletion confirmation when it ends.

If full masters leaving the studio is not acceptable, the specialist could instead work from the color-target frames plus crops of non-text areas such as paper margins and blank versos. This costs some color accuracy, but no letter content would leave the studio.

**2. Retention and deletion**

"Retained for quality control" is open-ended as drafted. We'd replace it with fixed periods:

| Stage | Timing | What happens |
|---|---|---|
| Correction window | Days 0–10 after each batch is delivered | Working files are kept, with access limited to named studio staff, so we can correct and rescan |
| Active deletion | Day 10 | Working files and the specialist's copies are deleted from active systems, and we confirm in writing |
| Backup expiry | Up to 45 days after active deletion | Backups rotate out automatically and are not accessed except for disaster recovery |
| Final certification | Day 55 at the latest | We certify in writing that no copies remain |

If the archive raises a correction request late in the window, we'd ask that the ten days restart for the affected files only.

**3. Publicity**

We accept the written-consent requirement as drafted. Under it, we'd ask for consent now, in principle, to one anonymized process image showing equipment and handling. It would show no legible text, names, handwriting or identifiable donor material. The archive would approve the specific image in writing before any use and could refuse it.

**What we need from you**

- Whether master-image access for the specialist is acceptable, or whether you'd prefer the targets-and-crops alternative.
- Whether the 10-day and 45-day periods fit the archive's donor obligations.
- Whether pre-approval of a specific process image is workable.

We propose the following terms for the signed schedule.

1. **Specialist access.** The archive will identify two restricted collections by batch ID. Only named studio staff may view their letters or images. For those batches, the specialist may use the archive’s calibration sheet. For other first-batch materials, the archive may also approve specific masked images or crops in writing. The studio must remove handwriting, identifying content and identifying metadata before the specialist sees a file. Master images stay with the studio. Please name the specialist in the schedule and retain your proposed limits on purpose, confidentiality, studio liability and prior written approval for any additional subcontractor.

2. **Retention and deletion.** We accept ten calendar days from each batch delivery for corrections, with access limited to named studio staff. The specialist must delete its copies when calibration ends or by day 10, whichever comes first, and provide written confirmation. A correction request may extend retention only for the affected files, with a new deletion date agreed in writing. The studio must confirm active deletion by batch and include the specialist’s confirmation where applicable. We propose that all backup copies expire **within 30 calendar days of delivery**, with final written certification by that date. During that period, backups may be accessed only for disaster recovery, and any restored files already due for deletion must be deleted again.

3. **Incident contact.** Each party will list a monitored email address and phone number in the schedule. The studio must alert the archive without delay on discovering suspected loss, unauthorized access or disclosure, including at the specialist. The first notice should identify the affected batches if known and the containment steps taken. Please send the studio’s contact details for the schedule.

4. **Publicity.** We can consider an equipment-only photograph taken with all donor materials out of frame and no files or identifying details visible on screens or labels. Please submit the exact image, caption and intended use for written approval before publication. No consent is granted in principle for a handling image.

**Outstanding exception.** Please confirm whether the studio can meet the 30-day backup deadline, including for files under correction. If a system requires longer, identify the affected copies, the shortest achievable expiry and whether those files can be excluded from backup. Any longer period needs express written agreement before the affected batch is processed.

Items 1 to 3 are agreed with small additions, but **the studio cannot meet the 30-day backup deadline**. The backup answer and a variation on the publicity photograph are the two points that need your reply.

**Outstanding exception: backups**

- **Affected copies:** all working files, since they are captured in the studio's routine backups while they sit on active systems.
- **Shortest achievable expiry:** backups rotate on a fixed 45-day cycle. A file deleted from active systems on day 10 may sit in a backup made that day, so the last backup copy expires by day 55 after delivery.
- **Files under correction:** the same 45 days runs from the extended deletion date agreed in writing, for those files only.
- **Exclusion from backup:** I can't confirm this today. I will ask the studio whether the two restricted batches can be held on storage excluded from backup, and give you a written answer before either batch is processed.

We therefore ask for express written agreement to the following:

- Backups expire no later than 45 days after active deletion (day 55 from delivery), with written certification by batch on that date.
- Your conditions apply throughout: access for disaster recovery only, and any restored file already due for deletion is deleted again.
- The studio notifies the archive of any restore that touches these batches.

If day 55 is unacceptable for the restricted collections, those two batches wait until the exclusion question is answered.

**1. Specialist access: agreed**

Master images stay with the studio. The specialist uses the archive's calibration sheet for the restricted batches, and only archive-approved masked images or crops for the other first-batch material. Handwriting, identifying content and identifying metadata are removed first. The limits on purpose, confidentiality, studio liability and additional subcontractors stay as proposed.

- **Approval timing:** crop approvals fall inside the ten-day correction window. We ask that the archive either answer requests within two business days, or pre-approve a category in the schedule: color-target frames and blank margins or versos with no writing.
- **Specialist's name:** the studio will supply the legal name for the schedule before signature.

**2. Retention and deletion: agreed apart from the backup date**

We accept ten calendar days from delivery, the specialist's deletion at the end of calibration or day 10 (whichever is first) with written confirmation, extensions for affected files only, and deletion confirmed by batch.

**3. Incident contact: agreed**

The specialist will be bound to report any suspected incident to the studio immediately, so the studio can alert the archive without delay. The studio will supply its monitored email address and phone number for the schedule along with the specialist's name.

**4. Publicity: agreed, with one variation to consider**

We accept that there is no consent in principle and no handling image of donor material. The studio will submit the exact image, caption and intended use for written approval before any publication.

The variation is whether the photograph may show the equipment with a studio-owned stand-in document on the scanner, so that it shows the process. The stand-in would be identified to you with the submission, and no archive material would be in the room when the photograph is taken. If not, we will work with equipment-only.

**Backups.** For batches outside the two restricted collections, the archive expressly agrees to backup expiry within 45 calendar days after active deletion. With active deletion on day 10, final written certification is due by day 55 after delivery. If both parties agree in writing to a later deletion date for specific files under correction, the studio will certify deletion of those files within 45 days of that date. The original deadline holds for the rest of the batch. Backups may be accessed only for disaster recovery. The studio will notify the archive of any restore affecting pilot files and promptly delete any restored files already due for deletion.

**Restricted collections.** The backup exception does not extend to these two collections. Please mark their batch IDs on hold in the schedule. If the studio confirms in writing that their files can be excluded from routine backups throughout processing, including corrections, the archive can release the batches in writing under the 30-day final certification deadline. If exclusion is unavailable, the batches stay on hold pending a separate written agreement. The other batches can proceed under the agreed terms.

**Specialist approvals.** The archive will answer each request within two business days of receiving the exact masked images or crops proposed for review. Access requires affirmative written approval for those files. For the restricted batches, the specialist may see only the archive’s calibration sheet. Please enter the specialist’s legal name and both parties’ monitored incident contacts before signature.

**Publicity.** Please use the equipment-only option, with the scanner empty, no archive material in the room and no identifying details visible. The archive will review the exact photograph, caption and intended use. Publication requires the archive’s written approval.

The studio agrees to all four points as you set them out, so the schedule can be drawn up for signature on that basis.
